newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fort Bonifacio listing unlikely in 1997 -First Pac.
newsitem.headline: Fort Bonifacio listing unlikely in 1997 -First Pac.

text.p: First Pacific Co Ltd said on Wednesday it is unlikely to list its Fort Bonifacio Development Corp unit this year due to recent negative investor sentiment towards the real estate market in the Philippines.

"I don't think it will happen. They don't need the money," First Pacific managing director Manuel Pangilinan told Reuters in an interview. "You are going to be pricing it at a stage when there is rather poor sentiment in the market."
Pangilinan said a listing might also send the "wrong signal" to the market that Fort Bonifacio needed cash which he said was not the case.
"The project has no debt. It has significant cash balances at this point in time - over two billion pesos," he said.
Pangilinan said in March that it was planning to list two of its Philippine units - Smart Communications in June or July this year and Fort Bonifacio during the year.
But the Philippine stock market has suffered a steep decline since reaching a record high in February and property stocks have taken a beating by fears of a meltdown in the real estate market.
Pangilinan said First Pacific hoped to list Smart Communications in August or September but thought it better to "preserve the value" of Fort Bonifacio.

He said Fort Bonifacio would get more cash with the sale of the 64-hectare sports and recreation area within Fort Bonifacio. The company signed a letter of intent in March to sell a 75 percent interest in the area to Fort McKinley Holdings Corp for 20.28 billion pesos.

"First Pacific has nothing to gain (from the Fort Bonifacio float) except for an exceptional profit which could arise from the flotation which we don't regard as a measure of performance of the group," said Pangilinan.
